And honestly after seeing and eating that burger I don't think I'd be coming to this place again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointed

As locals, we have been coming to Fairhill Café since it reopened two years ago. Recently, I arranged to meet a friend for lunch and was told admission was now $37pp. We were then confronted with the new prices, including $24 for a ham and cheese toastie. With our little outing exceeding $150 for 1 adult & 2 children, we simply won’t be returning.

Nevertheless, we paid to enter and hoped feeding the baby goats would soften the blow. We rushed through lunch to make the 12:30pm feeding, only to be told that 1 bottle had to be shared between 6 of us as there weren’t enough. Understandably, this left 4 children under 6 very upset.

With all activities taking place in the morning, we didn’t get the full experience we had paid for. It’s sad to see the business increasingly aimed at tourists and high-spending visitors rather than the local community like it once was.

To your ever-changing response: being “privately cared for and publicly shared” is the definition of a business. This is not a charity organisation “rescuing Fairhill from closure” as you claim.

By your own admission, your business model is now targeting a higher-net-worth clientele to generate greater profit. That inevitably changes who the experience is accessible and appealing to hence my review.

Continuing to update your response to invalidate my review only reinforces the perception that generating revenue and protecting your public image matters more than improving concerns of local families with genuine care.

One of the worst experiences I've ever had hiring a professional service.

I paid for certified translations expecting to simply receive the agreed-upon work (within 48 hours of requesting it) and have the matter resolved normally. Instead, I ended up facing arguments about money, extortionate demands for another payment (much higher than agreed upon), an initial refusal to return 2000 AUD (the initial 50%), and a one-hour ultimatum.

Among the messages I received were: “I’m going to report you, it’s a scam,” “I’ll decide for you in an hour,” and later, that they would keep my money as credit if I didn’t agree to their financial demands.

Finally, Guillermo Ramos agreed to return my money, but then his behavior was even worse. After the refund, I received direct insults.

I’m not exaggerating or making this up. It’s written in the messages I received, and I have screenshots.

There can be business disagreements between client and provider, but I don’t consider it normal for a professional to respond to a financial dispute with ultimatums, threats to report the client, and then personal insults.

After this experience, I personally would never use this service again. I would advise anyone thinking of hiring them to think twice.

This isn’t the first time this maladjusted potential scammer has done this. Now, for my peace of mind, I will report him directly to NAATI.

one_star_reviews.text:
Incredibly disappointing experience and honestly not worth the drive.

I visited The Western Ranch on Saturday, 3 October, genuinely excited and ready to spend decent money on a full riding and western outfit. Instead, I found a very small shop with extremely limited stock.

The men’s range was basically nonexistent. There may have been 10–15 pairs of pants in total, with hardly any sizes to choose from. The store clearly carries more women’s clothing, but even that range was surprisingly limited.

The customer service was probably the worst part. We were in the shop for around 15–20 minutes, and the lady working there spent virtually the entire time standing at the counter chatting with someone. She wasn’t serving them or helping with a purchase — they were simply having a conversation while other customers were being ignored.

She clearly saw me going through the limited stock, looking around and struggling to find anything suitable, yet never once came over or even asked if I needed help. When I eventually had to approach her and ask a question myself, the response was cold and dismissive, like having a customer ask for assistance was an inconvenience.

I left completely disappointed and went to Horseland Richmond instead — massive difference. Much bigger store, plenty of stock and brands, and I ended up spending around $1,000 there.

For somewhere I was genuinely excited to visit, The Western Ranch was a huge letdown. Definitely not worth making the drive for.

For a restaurant operating at Crown Sydney, we expected a much higher standard of food, service and professionalism.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience at Domino’s Pallara QLD 4110, particularly because of the way I was treated by the manager.

I have made several complaints previously regarding the service and the quality of the pizzas, but unfortunately, none of those concerns appear to have been taken seriously or properly addressed.

Instead of trying to resolve the issues professionally, my recent experience became even more concerning.

For this particular order, I specifically requested 2 Large Deep Pan Spicy Pepper Paneer pizzas and 1 Large Thin & Crispy Spicy Pepper Paneer pizza. Despite making the request clearly, the store prepared all three pizzas as Classic Crust.

What is even more frustrating is that nobody bothered to properly confirm the order with me before preparing it. I was told by the manager during pickup that they had called me, but that was not true. The store only contacted me after the pizzas had already been made, and they had proceeded with preparing the pizzas without getting my confirmation or permission.

When I arrived to collect the order, instead of trying to find a reasonable solution, the manager was extremely rude, disrespectful and unprofessional. The manager was apparently more interested in cancelling my order and telling me to go somewhere else rather than listening to my concern and resolving a very simple customer service issue.

I was even told, “Don’t come to my store again,” because I had previously raised complaints about the service and pizza quality. I was also told to go to another Domino’s store, and this was said in front of other people.

This kind of behaviour is completely unacceptable from someone representing a major brand like Domino’s. Customers have every right to raise genuine complaints when they receive poor service or an order that does not match what they requested. Making complaints should not result in a customer being treated disrespectfully or being told that they are no longer welcome at a store.

I chose not to argue with the manager at the time. I did not say anything disrespectful back because I have enough self-respect to walk away from an unnecessary confrontation. However, staying quiet should not be mistaken for accepting this behaviour.

The bigger concern for me is the complete lack of professionalism and accountability. Mistakes can happen in any business. If the store had simply acknowledged the mistake, apologised and tried to resolve it, I would have understood. Instead, the situation was made much worse by the way I was spoken to and treated.

I am therefore asking Domino’s Pallara management, the store owner/franchisee and Domino’s higher management to seriously investigate this incident, including the previous complaints I have made, the order details, the communication records and the conduct of the manager involved.

Customers should not be made to feel unwelcome simply because they have raised legitimate concerns about the service they received.

I hope Domino’s takes this feedback seriously and provides appropriate training and accountability to ensure that other customers are not treated in the same manner.

This is not simply about a pizza being made with the wrong crust. It is about respect, customer service, professionalism and how a customer is treated when something goes wrong.

I would appreciate a proper response from Domino’s higher management rather than another generic response or an ignored complaint.

one_star_reviews.text:
This shop is excellent when it comes to providing recommendations and offering a range of options, but unfortunately, where it falls short, quite significantly, is customer service.
The older gentleman who runs the shop is incredible. However, my experience with the younger employee who assists in the store was very disappointing.
I have run more than 10 marathons, several ultras, 50+ half marathons, and am currently training for triathlon. The day before a half marathon, I went into the shop to purchase a new pair of running shoes, expecting an active conversation about what I was training for, my running history, and what I needed from a shoe.
Instead, it seemed to be assumed that I was only training for a 5K and therefore needed beginner-level shoes. There is absolutely nothing wrong with training for a 5K or being a beginner, but the issue was that I was never asked any questions about my experience, training, or goals before that assumption was made.
What made the experience particularly disappointing was that, while I was still deliberating and planning to purchase the shoes, another man came into the shop. The employee immediately asked him what times he was running, what he was training for, and other questions about his running.
The contrast was hard to ignore.
This happened a few months ago, but it has stayed on my mind. In a sport and culture that should be actively encouraging women and recognising them as serious athletes, it was extremely disappointing to feel that my experience and goals were assumed rather than explored.
The shop clearly has the knowledge and expertise to provide excellent advice, but that needs to be matched with consistent customer service and a willingness to ask questions before making assumptions.
I wouldn’t return, and while I initially thought word of mouth was enough, I felt it was important to share my experience.

Didn’t even get anything and didn’t even pay anything, so I can’t complain as you get nothing for nothing.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing after-sales experience

I purchased a Toyota LandCruiser 300 from Cavalo Prestige as an interstate buyer, relying on the information and promises provided to me by their salesperson during the purchase process. Unfortunately, my experience after the sale has been extremely disappointing.

After bringing the vehicle back to South Australia, I discovered a discrepancy with the vehicle’s year. The vehicle was represented to me as a 2024 LandCruiser, while the registration records show it as a 2023 vehicle. This is not a minor detail when purchasing a vehicle of this value.

I also discovered missing service history, despite being told about the vehicle’s service history before purchasing. I trusted the information provided by the dealership rather than expecting that every verbal representation would later need to be proven in writing.

When I raised these issues with Cavalo Prestige, I was asked to provide written proof of what their salesperson had promised me. I find this extremely disappointing because the salesperson who dealt with me has since left the company, and I cannot simply produce a written document for every verbal conversation we had. From my perspective, I purchased the vehicle based on the representations made to me by their staff and trusted the dealership.

What has been even more disappointing is the lack of meaningful after-sales support and accountability. Instead of taking ownership of the concerns and properly investigating what was discussed at the time of sale, I have been repeatedly asked to prove conversations that took place verbally.

I was an interstate buyer who travelled and purchased the vehicle based on the information provided by the dealership. I expected a much higher level of transparency and customer support after spending this amount of money.

My experience has been that getting assistance after the sale has been extremely difficult. Anyone considering purchasing from Cavalo Prestige should make sure that every representation, promise, service-history detail and vehicle-year detail is confirmed in writing before handing over any money.

I am sharing this review based on my own experience so other buyers can make their own informed decision and understand the importance of getting everything documented before purchasing.

I would not recommend buying from Cavalo Prestige based on my experience.

Three weeks ago, I purchased what was represented to me as a 2024 Toyota LandCruiser 300. After bringing the vehicle back to South Australia and registering it, I discovered it was recorded as a 2023 model, which was very disappointing as there is a one-year difference.

When the vehicle was delivered, it looked spotless because it had been professionally detailed. However, after washing it for the first time a week later, I noticed numerous paint imperfections across the roof and bonnet. I also found rust spots in multiple areas around the vehicle that were not apparent at delivery.

I raised these concerns with a member of the Cavalo Prestige team shortly after discovering them, but so far I have not received any response or assistance. The lack of after-sales support has been extremely disappointing.

I’m sharing my experience so that other buyers take the time to thoroughly inspect any vehicle before purchasing, including checking the model year, paint condition, and overall bodywork, rather than relying solely on how the car looks when it has just been detailed.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐️1 star – unfortunately, I absolutely cannot recommend this dealership.

I personally did not buy a car from this dealership, but I have witnessed all the stress and drama my sister has been going through since purchasing her car there.

Everything was great until she signed the contract. But as soon as the paperwork was signed, their attitude completely changed. Less than two weeks later, my sister was already back at the dealership because of problems with the car – and since then, it has turned into an almost 3-month-long battle.

What makes the situation even more frustrating is that some of these problems were already present when the car was sold to her. For example, the doors and windows are not properly sealed. This is obviously not something we could have known or reasonably noticed during a normal viewing before buying the car. These problems only became apparent afterwards.

Had my sister known about these issues before signing the contract, she would not have bought the car. She made her decision believing she was buying a car without these kinds of existing problems.

Since then, she has repeatedly been sent away. One time she was told that nothing could be repaired, another time she was told that the issue was not covered by the warranty – even though she specifically paid extra for a warranty. To this day, there is still no proper solution.

What makes this even more disappointing is what happened after we posted our first reviews. Suddenly, we received a response and were told that we needed to delete our reviews first. We did exactly that, trusting that they would finally take the situation seriously and help resolve the problem.

And what happened after we deleted them? My sister was ignored AGAIN. Nothing has been properly resolved, and the situation is still ongoing.

So this time, this review will stay up until this matter is actually dealt with. If the dealership finally resolves the issue properly, I will of course update my review accordingly.

I simply do not think it is acceptable to treat customers like this after they have purchased a car. Based on what we have experienced, I especially would not recommend this dealership to anyone who does not know much about cars themselves. Please be extremely careful, ask questions, and make sure you fully understand what you are buying and what is actually covered by the warranty.

As for the additional warranty she paid for? Based on our experience so far, we are seriously questioning what exactly she paid for.

Buying a car should not turn into a months-long battle just to be taken seriously as a customer – especially when problems that were already present at the time of purchase only become apparent afterwards.

⭐️ 1 Star – Buyer left to deal with major problems alone

An extremely disappointing experience with this dealer.

I bought a Holden Captiva and shortly thereafter had to contend with numerous serious issues. These include, among other things, water ingress through several doors, warning lights, problems with the tailgate indicator, significant anomalies regarding fuel consumption and driving range, and other technical faults.

What particularly frustrates me is that instead of taking these issues seriously, the dealer repeatedly downplays them or dismisses them as "wear-and-tear items" or claims they aren't covered by the warranty. To me, this is not an acceptable solution.

I have contacted the dealer multiple times via email and phone, and have even visited the premises in person on several occasions. Despite this, I am consistently ignored or offered no reasonable solution.

I have since explicitly demanded a reversal of the sale—or the return of the vehicle—as I believe I am entitled to specific consumer rights under Australian Consumer Law. The dealer’s response essentially amounts to: "We won't take the car back; a sale is a sale."

In my opinion, this is not how customers should be treated.

I have given the dealer more than enough opportunity to resolve the matter voluntarily and sensibly. Instead, in my experience, the problems are downplayed and my attempts to make contact are sometimes ignored.

I paid for a vehicle without expecting to be confronted with so many problems and so much additional stress immediately after the purchase.

When a dealer abandons their customers like this after a sale—despite repeated notifications of serious issues—it leaves a very poor impression on me.

My advice to anyone looking to buy a vehicle here: Have the vehicle thoroughly inspected by an independent party before purchasing, document every defect, and get all statements and promises in writing. I will continue to pursue my rights as a consumer and continue to expect a serious resolution to this matter.and they don't abide by Australian laws

I visited the Andar Sydney Westfield store today intending to purchase two pairs of pants for an upcoming trip. I had already researched the products online and knew exactly what I wanted to try and potentially purchase.

As the store was very quiet, I asked a staff member if I could try the Airywin Wide Pants in both the long and short lengths, in black and maintain view colours in size Large, as well as the Airyfit Wide Pants in black, size Large.

From the beginning, the staff member provided me with a light beige colour pant on the floor to try. I explained that I specifically wanted to try the black colour because I would never purchase light-coloured pants and wanted to see how the actual colour I intended to buy looked on me.

To my surprise, I was told that I could only try the sizes and colours currently displayed on the shop floor, and that I was not allowed to try the stock kept at the back of the store unless I had already paid for it.

I found this extremely confusing and disappointing. I have never encountered this kind of fitting policy at a retail store in Australia or elsewhere. As a customer, I believe it is completely reasonable to want to try the actual colour and style I am considering purchasing, particularly when the store has the stock available.

The experience made me feel very uncomfortable and disappointed with the level of customer service. I decided not to proceed with the purchase in-store and left the shop.

I ended up having to purchase the items online instead.

I had a very different expectation of the Andar brand after researching the products beforehand. Unfortunately, the in-store experience has left me quite disappointed, and I hope the management can review this policy and the way customers are assisted in the future.If you want, I can also make it stronger and more impactful, particularly highlighting how unreasonable it is to ask customers to pay before being allowed to try the actual colour/stock they want.

one_star_reviews.text:
This restaurant, no joke, has probably the worst service out of any restaurant I have been to in my life.

When I entered, the restaurant was not packed at all. Despite this, the owner/chef, cooks, and servers were constantly arguing as I could see and hear from the whole other side of the restaurant. The food took an extremely lengthy period of time to come - and that is the case even when they remembered our orders - lol!

The servers were quite bad in terms of remembering normal, mundane requests, and they had to be explicitly requested by us to replenish basic table items, whether it be cutlery, dishes, or water.

Now, the food - the purpose of a restaurant - was quite subpar for the price. The bread and butter, and a few other mains were “extra ordinary”tasting (not extraordinary). The standout dishes were the bland, almost tasteless barramundi, and the Wagyu truffle croquettes which were comparable to a bite of a burger with overcooked minced beef left to sit for hours. Overall, all dishes tasted like food for food’s sake - lacking exquisite flavour and merely eaten as human nourishment - like many cheap, subpar food-court-style foods. In simpler words; if it was hungry, and it was there, I would eat it. Furthermore, many dishes used the same sauces - I mean sure, base ingredients are good - but not really

In short, I’ve had better service at HK-style cafes (notorious for their inhospitality), and the food here at Bellevue is not special at all, and I mean that.

P.S. can this restaurant also stop botting 5 star reviews? it’s quite obvious and misleading to others who fell into the trap - like how i did.

Absolutely horrendous. One of the worst dining experiences I’ve had in a long time.

From the second we arrived, there was zero service, zero attention and zero basic hospitality. We were constantly ignored and had to keep trying to get someone’s attention.

We ordered a $110 bottle of French rose which took forever to come out. When the waitress finally brought it over, she tried to pass off a 2026 South Australian rose as the bottle we ordered. We pointed out that it wasn’t what we ordered and she then told us they didn’t have it and that this was the only rose they had. It’s a French restaurant, so that’s a blatant why she was just trying to get rid of it and thought we wouldn’t know.

I asked her how much the Adelaide wine was, and instead of answering me, she asked me how much the French one we originally ordered was…. I said I couldn’t remember. She wanted to say they were the same price.

Sorry, but I’m not paying $110 for a 2026 Adelaide rose when I ordered a French bottle. And this is a French restaurant by the way. How does a French restaurant not have French wine? Total lie. There is literally an entire cellar of wine behind the bar, but  apparently this was the “only rose” they had.

Then 40 minutes in and we still hadn’t even been served a drink. We ordered drinks when we arrived. Forty minutes later, nothing.

We specifically asked for all of the food to come out together. Obviously that didn’t happen either.

First thing to arrive was the tuna tataki. The tuna was slimy as hell, horribly cut and looked like it had been hacked apart by a child with plastic scissors. It was also swimming in a ridiculous amount of sauce that was completely unnecessary and just ruined it.

Then the asparagus came out. They had been halved to make it look like more and tasted like previously frozen, soggy vegetables. No freshness, no texture, nothing.

Then the $70 medium rare steak. Three (???) edible pieces of overcooked steak, surrounded by a ridiculous amount of fat. And again, cut so badly it looked like a child had used plastic scissors on it.

At this point the whole meal felt like some sort of horrendous experiment.

There is 0% French about this place and 0% class.

The prices and the location are premium. Woolloomooloo is an expensive area and I can only imagine what the rent on this place is, but they are completely wasting the spot.

I honestly cannot see this place lasting more than a couple of months if this is the standard they are operating at.

The best and only good part of the entire meal was the beer.

Absolutely shocking from start to finish.

Overall, the food was overpriced for the quality, the service was poor, and the atmosphere wasn't pleasant.

I honestly can't recommend this place based on my experience. If you're looking for good customer service, quality ingredients and properly prepared food, I'd look elsewhere.

Very disappointing. End of story.

I am formally requesting that the $200 charge be refunded and that this matter be reviewed as a warranty issue.

I have both receipts for the previous repair and the current repair. When my iPhone 17 Pro was repaired in August, I was specifically advised that the repair was covered by warranty and that defects involving the display/touch would be covered.

Yesterday, the phone remained fully operational — I could receive calls and feel the phone vibrating — however the display completely stopped working and the screen was not showing anything.

I have now been charged a further $200, despite the fact that I was given a warranty on the original repair. I have been told that the reason for this is a small hairline fracture on the screen protector.

I do not accept that the existence of a hairline fracture on a screen protector, by itself, establishes that the LCD/display failure was caused by physical damage. The screen protector is separate from the LCD/display that was repaired.

I was also extremely disappointed by the way I was spoken to when I raised this issue. Being told that I have “no common sense” and that I either pay the $200 or you will not repair my phone is not an appropriate way to deal with a customer who is raising a legitimate warranty concern.

If you are refusing to honour the warranty, please provide me in writing:

• the specific warranty term you are relying upon;
• the exact component that has failed;
• the reason you have determined that the failure was caused by the hairline fracture;
• any evidence supporting that determination; and
• why the issue is not being treated as a warranty repair.

I have retained both receipts and will retain all correspondence relating to this matter.

I am requesting that the $200 charge be refunded to me and that this matter be dealt with under the warranty provided with the August repair.

If the $200 is not refunded and the warranty issue is not appropriately resolved, I will be taking the matter to NSW Fair Trading/Consumer Law and providing them with both receipts, the warranty information and our correspondence as evidence.

I would prefer to resolve this directly with you, but I am not prepared to accept being charged $200 for an issue that I was specifically told would be covered under the warranty.

20 minutes later… FOOD.

At this point, we had been sitting there for over an hour and had experienced enough character development to qualify for a Netflix series.

The most impressive part? Not once did anyone proactively come over to explain the delay or check on us. We had to chase everything ourselves.

The ONE thing they did do was offer us a complimentary tiramisu at the end, which was appreciated - although by that stage, the tiramisu felt less like dessert and more like compensation for the emotional damage.

By the time the mains arrived, we weren’t sure whether to eat them or frame them as historical artefacts.

Lovely restaurant if you’re looking to spend your evening waiting, wondering and developing a deep personal relationship with the phrase “they’re coming.”

Would not recommend unless you have absolutely nowhere else to be. 🍝

I came for Italian food and apparently stayed long enough to complete a small Italian pilgrimage.

The wait for the food was very long, which gave me plenty of time to contemplate life, the harbour, and whether my dinner had actually left the kitchen.

The prosciutto pizza was particularly memorable. There was so much rocket on it that I briefly wondered whether I had accidentally ordered a salad with a small amount of pizza underneath. Somewhere beneath the mountain of rocket was a touch of prosciutto, bravely fighting for recognition.

The carbonara arrived looking the part, but unfortunately the flavour seemed to have taken the night off. Calling it bland would almost be giving it too much personality.

The location is fantastic, but unfortunately the view of Circular Quay did more for my appetite than the food did.

2 stars for the location and the entertainment value of discovering just how much rocket can physically fit on a pizza. 🌿🍕

Edit: Hi Thrifter, my review reflects my genuine experience as a customer coming in on my birthday month, and I stand by what I wrote. I would have preferred a professional response addressing my concern rather than having my honesty questioned publicly.

I want to clarify my concerns because I feel that your response has focused primarily on the 2:45pm fitting-room policy, when that was not the entirety of what I raised. I acknowledge that you have a closing time for your fitting rooms and that this policy may apply to all customers. I am not alleging that the existence of that policy is discriminatory. My concern is the way my friends and I were treated in connection with that policy and throughout our visit, particularly in comparison with our friend who was shopping with us and other customers who entered the store during the same period. We spent approximately $720 in your store. Despite this, we were not greeted when entering until my friend greeted your staff, we were repeatedly reminded about the fitting-room closure despite having already acknowledged it, experienced what we perceived as dismissive and hostile interactions. As well as, were treated differently at the point of purchase.

For example, my friend was not offered a bag and had to request one and pack our own purchases, whereas my  friend was offered a bag and had her belongings packed for her. We also observed staff interacting more warmly with other customers entering the store while our group was being rushed.
When I asked whether we could return an item if it did not fit because we were unable to use the fitting rooms, I was interrupted and told that the rooms were closed. My friend then clarified the question. Asking if we could return items that do not fit due to the policy on the changing rooms.

These circumstances, taken together, caused us to feel that we were being treated differently because of our race. I want to address your statement that we were apparently "smiling" on CCTV. Continuing to shop, speaking with friends or smiling during an interaction does not demonstrate that any person was   or would be comfortable with the treatment they were receiving. People do not have to appear visibly distressed on CCTV for their experience of discrimination or mistreatment to be genuine. More importantly, I am not asking you to determine my feelings from CCTV. I am asking you to review the actual conduct captured on CCTV and compare how the customers in our group were treated with how other customers were treated. BEWARE!

This review relates to my experience with Morale Patches, the online store associated with this business.

I placed an order for an item that was advertised as being in stock. I contacted the business on 31 August 2026 regarding the status of the order and followed up again on 5 September requesting a refund. Despite those attempts to contact them, I received no response, no meaningful update, no refund, and the item was never dispatched.

For several weeks, the business had my payment while I had neither the product I had ordered nor any explanation as to what was happening with the order.

After receiving no response, I eventually lodged a chargeback with my bank. It was only after I raised the chargeback that the business contacted me and processed a refund.

It was also only at this point - several weeks after I had placed the order - that I was finally told that the wholesaler could not supply the product, that there was no ETA for restocking, and therefore that the item I had ordered was not actually available to be supplied. This was particularly disappointing because the product had been advertised as being in stock when I placed and paid for the order.

What I found most frustrating was the difference in communication before and after the chargeback. My emails asking about an order I had already paid for, including my request for a refund, went unanswered. However, once I involved my bank and lodged a chargeback, I began receiving responses about the matter.

I advised the business that once the refund had been received and cleared, I would notify my bank so that the chargeback could be updated accordingly.

Despite this, I then received emails instructing me to cancel the chargeback by close of business the following day. I was told that I was “legally required” to cancel it immediately and was advised that, if I did not do so, I would be sent what the business described as a “Cease and Assist Letter”, charged their legal costs and a $25 chargeback fee, and that the matter would be lodged with police. The email also described the situation as a “fraudulent matter” and warned that their legal fees would be “very expensive”.

I found this response particularly concerning given the circumstances. I had only lodged the chargeback after several weeks without receiving the item, a response to my emails, or the refund I had requested. I had also already informed the business that I would advise my bank once their refund had been processed.

Had the business simply responded to my earlier emails and explained that the product was unavailable, this situation could likely have been resolved without a chargeback at all.

This review reflects my personal experience with this order and the communications I received from the business. I was disappointed by the lack of communication, the fact that an item advertised as being in stock could not actually be supplied, the delay in providing a refund, and the manner in which the business responded once I raised the matter with my bank.

Based on this experience, I found the handling of the matter very unprofessional and would not purchase from this business again.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Falcon Cargo to anyone looking for a reliable cargo service between Australia and Sri Lanka.

I have shopped at Woolworths Castle Hill Showground Village regularly since the store opened, often almost every day. After what occurred on 7 October at approximately 5:15pm, I will not be returning.

My family and I were using the self-service checkouts when the register indicated that staff assistance was required. A young blonde female staff member was working in the area. Despite us requesting assistance first, she attended to another customer who raised their hand after us.

When she eventually came over, her manner was dismissive and unnecessarily hostile. She swiped her staff card, offered no basic courtesy, and walked away with an attitude as though we had done something wrong simply because the checkout required staff authorisation.

We were polite, we had caused no issue, and there was absolutely no justification for being treated in that manner.

What concerns me most is the apparent belief that customers can be spoken to or treated with disrespect without consequence. That is a very dangerous attitude for any business to allow, particularly when staff are dealing directly with members of the public.

For clarity, I am documenting the exact date, approximate time, location and description of the staff member because I expect this incident to be taken seriously. Woolworths should have no difficulty identifying who was rostered in the self-service area at approximately 5:15pm on 7 October.

I would strongly suggest management review any available CCTV and staffing records relating to this incident.

Good customer service is not an optional extra. Customers are entitled to be treated with basic courtesy and respect.

This experience has permanently changed my view of this store. I have supported this particular Woolworths since it opened, but I will now take my business elsewhere.

I am also considering escalating the matter through Woolworths’ formal complaints process and any other appropriate avenues if I am not satisfied that the incident has been properly addressed.

Businesses should never assume that a customer will simply accept unacceptable treatment and disappear quietly.

I said I wanted white, then she gave a follow up question asking FULL WHITE? To which I thought the full white meant no design just plain, so I said YES. Then when it got to painting the nail, the second she painted the entire nail white, I stopped her. Even when she would 'lightly guide my hand' she would yank my hand so aggressively.

3. I also understand customer priority, bookings, and even time management. However this lady doesn't. It's not my fault that she probably did not take into account time. But when another customer who apparently had a booking walked in, she quickly got up, grabbed her stuff and relocated to a different table to serve this new customer without even a single word said to me. Only talking to the male employee saying that the lady booked with her. Still nothing being said to me. So I took it as she was gonna take a little while with the new client. Overpriced and very disappointing — $40 with coffee

Unfortunately, this was one of the most disappointing brunches I’ve had.

The brisket was extremely dry and rubbery, with almost no flavour. There was very little sauce, no noticeable seasoning or spices, and the meat itself was quite bland. The kale was also basically just steamed greens with no real seasoning. To make things worse, there were random large grains of salt throughout the dish, so every now and then I would bite into an unexpectedly very salty piece. It didn’t work with the dish at all.

The scrambled eggs were more like a thin egg sheet than properly cooked scrambled eggs.

The sausage was another issue. It had an unpleasant smell and taste. After one bite, I actually had to look back at the menu to check whether it was a lamb sausage because the flavour was so unusual. I ended up leaving more than half of it.

For $32 for the plate, and around $40 including coffee, I honestly couldn’t understand the price. At this price point, I expect much more flavour, seasoning and attention to the food.

You need to put flavour on the plate.

I couldn’t finish the meal and ended up going somewhere else to have lunch afterwards.

Unfortunately, I wouldn’t come back.

My family and I were assured by the clinical care staff at Arcare Aranda that my mother would be properly cared for as she had complex clinical needs. Unfortunately, based on my experience of her 2 months care in 2026, I believe those assurances were not met.

My concerns included significant weight loss and what I understood to be inadequate monitoring of her weight. I was also concerned about her hygiene, as well as the management of her pressure sores. In addition, requests for specialist clinical support—including a dietitian and physiotherapist—did not receive adequate responses.

Because of the weight loss and my concerns for her physical and psychological wellbeing, I asked for my mother to be transported to North Canberra Hospital. She had also told me that she no longer wanted to remain at the facility.

I requested my mother’s clinical care records from the clinical team at Arcare Aranda on her behalf, but a number of requested records were not provided to me.

This review reflects my experience, and based on that experience, I would not recommend Arcare Aranda to families seeking aged care for a loved one.

one_star_reviews.text:
I interacted with Ms Foster's office to request advocacy in March 2026 through May 2026 regarding my mother, who has now passed.

Ms Foster's office was extremely slow to act and made several professional mistakes. I feel the amount of time that passed without action is unforgivable, especially since I did all of the hard work for them.

My feedback on interacting with Ms Foster's office is that I feel there is a large disconnect between Ms Foster's brand and image, and the people she has chosen to hire in her office, who ultimately are a representation of her.

In particular, I feel that the staff member who was the point of contact for my case could not truly understand and empathise with my family's circumstances and advocate for my family to the best of their ability.

I feel that the quality of responses received reflected someone who grew up with a lot of privilege outside of Mulgrave and were totally disconnected with the lives of constituents in one of Victoria's longstanding disadvantaged electorates.

It left a bad taste in my mouth, to be a well-educated person with lived experiences and advocacy experience, and still have been bound by this staff member who was not willing to fight and push in the manner that someone who was working for Ms Foster's office should have done.

While I can understand that the MP's office is small, I feel that at some point, my case should have been directly referred to a professional advocate, who would have been able to provide the level of attention that my case warranted whilst minimising the amount of burnout on myself, which I am still recovering from.

It bodes poorly when Labor staff/volunteers are knocking on my family's door to campaign for Ms Foster, when there have been multiple opportunities in the preceding months to show up for my family when it mattered most.

As someone who is progressive and operates through the world with logic, reasoning and facts, I should be voting for Labor on my own accord, but it's hard to see myself doing so when so many things in our electorate are not the way they should be.

Terrible service. I called this company out to diagnose a Truma UltraRapid that wasn't lighting. The technician spent a very short amount of time on-site before confidently telling me I needed a new PCB.

I ordered a new PCB, but there was absolutely no change in the unit’s behaviour; it has the exact same problem. Their invoice explicitly stated:
"Check truma hot water system
Test PCB
Found PCB faulty (Pull in solenoid not receiving power)
Replacement board is required."
I paid for their expertise and was given a definitive diagnosis that turned out to be completely wrong, or at least not the complete problem.

When I tried to consult with Gary about the issue, he was unhelpful and dismissive. He suggested the solenoid might have shorted out, but when I asked if the solenoid had actually been tested during the initial visit, he was short with his response, stating it was "within range" and pointing out that my invoice wasn't paid yet. I then received an email stating "We require immediate payment of this amount to avoid further action.", which I find completely unprofessional when the diagnosis I paid for appears incorrect or incomplete. I have a right to a service carried out with due care and skill, which this does not appear to have been.

Response to owners response:
Hi Gary, thank you for the response. To clarify, what was written as the diagnosis did not outline a multi-step "repair process" or mention any underlying issues; it explicitly stated: "Found PCB faulty... Replacement board is required." I did not choose to carry out only part of a job, I simply followed your definitive written diagnosis to the letter. Unfortunately, installing the new board resulted in absolutely no change to the unit's behaviour.

Furthermore, if the solenoid was tested on the day and found to be "within range" as you mentioned during our correspondence, it is difficult to understand how it could be the underlying cause.

While I understand electrical faults can be complex, I engaged your business for a professional diagnosis to avoid guesswork. To be threatened with further action over an invoice for an incorrect, or incomplete diagnosis feels unfair, especially when it resulted in the costly purchase of a part that did not fix the problem.

one_star_reviews.text:
9. The Most Frustrating Part

The most frustrating part was that after ending the relationship, we had to spend a significant amount of time working with our new agency to clean up, reconnect and understand accounts and assets that we believed should have remained under our company's control.

Instead of simply moving to a new agency and continuing to focus on our business, we had to spend considerable time dealing with account structures, access issues and tracking concerns.

10. Communication and Client Service

Our disappointment was not only related to advertising management.

We also found the communication frustrating at various stages of the relationship.

Some Account Managers came across to us as dismissive, and the response time was sometimes unacceptable.

On one occasion, we waited six days for a response to a single email.

When a client is paying an agency to manage an important part of their business, we believe timely communication, accountability and clear explanations are basic expectations.

11. Our Overall Experience

Our experience with Advisible and subsequently Aiims left us extremely disappointed and frustrated.

We engaged an advertising agency because we wanted professional management, better advertising performance and reliable conversion tracking.

Instead, after ending the relationship, we found ourselves spending significant time with a new agency trying to understand the previous account structure, address tracking concerns and regain appropriate access to our business assets.

The biggest lesson we took from this experience is that businesses should make sure their Google Ads, GA4, Google Business Profile, domain, Google Tag Manager and other important digital assets remain under accounts that the business itself controls.

We wish we had paid much more attention to this from the beginning.

This has been a very frustrating experience, particularly because so much time and energy had to be spent dealing with these issues after the relationship ended.

6. Difficulties Regaining Access After Ending the Relationship

After we clearly communicated that we no longer wished to continue the relationship, we still experienced difficulties obtaining full access to some of our Google Business Profile, GA4 and Google Ads assets.

At one point, the explanation provided to us was simply:

“This is company policy.”

For us, this was extremely frustrating.

These accounts are essential to running our business and working with other service providers. We expected the transition to a new agency to be straightforward, rather than having to spend significant time resolving access issues.

7. What We Discovered When Moving to a New Agency

We eventually engaged a new advertising agency and asked them to review our existing Google Ads setup in detail.

We wanted to understand how the account had been structured, where our advertisements had been appearing and how conversion tracking had been configured.

During this review, our new agency identified placements and conversion-related settings that raised significant concerns for us.

For example, one of the higher-traffic sources identified in the account was mobile app / gaming placements.

Another traffic source was labelled as an “Enquiry Form”, despite our website not having an enquiry form.

These findings made us question whether the account structure and traffic/conversion data had been configured in a way that accurately reflected our actual e-commerce business.

8. Conversion Tracking Concerns

Our new agency also identified issues with the way sales and conversion tracking had been configured.

For an e-commerce business, accurate conversion tracking is fundamental.

We were paying for professional advertising management with the expectation that our advertising performance would be measured accurately and that the data would allow us to make informed decisions about our advertising budget.

Instead, after moving agencies, we found ourselves having to investigate whether the historical conversion setup accurately represented what was actually happening on our website.

Extremely Disappointing Experience with Aiims

Our original advertising agreement was with Advisible, which was later merged into Aiims. Because of that, our experience with Aiims was not limited to the period after the merger — it also included the ongoing management of the accounts and systems that had originally been established under Advisible.

I am leaving this review separately because, from our perspective, the issues we experienced continued through the transition and ultimately became even more apparent when we tried to move to a new agency.

1. Constantly Changing Account Managers

Advisible was the company we originally signed with, and it was later merged into Aiims.

Throughout our time working with the business, we went through numerous Account Managers. The only Account Manager we felt was genuinely helpful and responsible in managing our account eventually left the company as well.

Every time a new Account Manager took over, we had to explain our business, products, priorities and advertising strategy again.

For a business paying an agency to manage an important part of its marketing, this made it very difficult to maintain consistency and build any meaningful understanding of our business.

2. Limited Visibility Into What Was Actually Being Done

Once our Google Ads account had been established, our overall experience was that there was very limited visibility into what was actually being changed or optimised.

When performance was good, we were generally told:

“The performance is good, just keep it going.”

When performance was poor, we were told:

“We have made some adjustments.”

or:

“We are still making adjustments and monitoring the results.”

Whenever we asked what had actually been changed, we often did not receive a clear explanation.

At one point, I asked that screenshots simply be provided so we could see what changes had been made. Even that was not provided.

Throughout this period, we continued paying the monthly management fee.

3. Limited Proactive Optimisation

Based on our experience, we did not see the level of consistent, proactive and in-depth optimisation that we expected from a professional advertising agency.

We expected the agency to actively analyse the account, identify problems, test different strategies and continuously look for opportunities to improve performance.

Instead, our experience often felt reactive rather than proactive — we would receive a report, be told that performance was either good or that adjustments had been made, and then be asked to wait for the results.

4. Account Structure and Digital Asset Management

One of the biggest issues became apparent when we decided to move to another advertising agency.

We discovered that our Google Ads, GA4, Google Business Profile, domain and other business assets had been connected and managed across different accounts and email addresses.

These are fundamental business assets that we expected our own company to retain clear ownership and administrative control over.

After moving to a new agency, we had to spend a significant amount of time trying to understand the existing structure, reconnect accounts and regain appropriate access and control.

Only during this process did we realise how complicated the existing setup had become.

5. Dispute Over “Intellectual Property”

One of the most difficult parts of the process was being told, when we requested access to our own accounts and assets, that some items were considered the agency's “intellectual property.”

This was extremely difficult for us to understand.

We had engaged the agency to manage our advertising. We had not understood that this meant the agency would retain control over business accounts or assets that we had created or were using to operate our business.

This raised serious concerns for us about how ownership and access to digital assets were handled during the relationship.

For more, see the next one.

1 star
DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME AND MONEY STAY AWAY FROM POLLN - THEY TAKE YOUR MONEY AND DISAPPEAR AND THEY DO NOT ANSWER THE PHONE

I have been a Polln patient for around two years, and my recent experience has been bad enough that I no longer have confidence in the service.

My consultation with Dr Asad was particularly disappointing. He joined approximately 15 minutes late, gave no apology or acknowledgment of the delay, and the consultation then felt extremely rushed. In my experience, his manner was dismissive and unfriendly, and I did not feel that he properly listened to or addressed my concerns. For a paid medical consultation, I expected basic professionalism, courtesy and adequate time to discuss my treatment.

What happened afterwards made the experience considerably worse. My Polln account continued to show existing prescriptions with 3/3 supplies remaining, yet I was suddenly unable to place an order. I contacted Polln because I was running out of medication and wanted the problem fixed. Instead of receiving a clear explanation of what had happened to my prescriptions, I received repeated responses saying that Dr Asad wanted either a GP health summary or access to my My Health Record before reviewing my treatment again.

I repeatedly explained that I was not asking for a new medication or a change in treatment. I was trying to understand why I could no longer access prescriptions already displayed in my account with supplies remaining. I eventually ran out of medication while trying to get a straight answer.

What frustrated me most was the lack of transparency. If a doctor has made a clinical decision affecting an existing prescription, the patient should be clearly told what has changed and why. Instead, I had to repeatedly ask whether my prescriptions were still valid, whether they had been placed on hold, and why my account continued showing them as available.

Polln’s support staff were polite, but the process itself has been extremely frustrating and poorly handled.

After being a patient for around two years, I did not expect a doctor to arrive late, rush through the consultation, communicate poorly, and then have my access to treatment interrupted without a clear explanation.

I have now made a formal complaint regarding Dr Asad’s consultation and the handling of my prescriptions.

Based on this experience, I cannot recommend Polln.

Id be careful with this childcare centre. In regards to my daughter attending here she was having upwards of 4, 5 hour gaps between feedings. She is 6 months old and that is actually  extremely concerning for her age. When i spoke to educators they tried to justify the feeding times but ended up agreeing to feed her every 3 hours. Then they called my wife and told her that I agreed to 3-5 hours which again is extremely bad for the health of a child and actually illegal in NSW.

I also expressed my wife's concern about the daycare oversleeping our child resulting in inability to sleep at home, to which their response was simply that they cant do anything about it because they do not wake sleeping children. Thats all well and good but you could easily keep her awake playing for longer and push back the sleep time especially considering we were advised by a doctor to wake her for feedings every 3 hours due to weight loss. I communicated this to them but they were very argumentative and disagreeable with me.

My daughter has sensitive skin when exposed to synthetic fabrics so we provided a cotton blanket and we were assured it would be used. Whenever we collect ted our bags the blanket was still folded the same way as when we provided it and when I questioned the staff they said they used their own in house cotton throw as opposed to mine. However when inspecting the photos provided by the daycare they were clearly handling her without one at all. They directly lied to me and my wife about it which is just unacceptable.

This daycare straight up refuses to feed infants solids. When provided we took photos of all the foods to see which were interacted with. Most were not touched and they were never heated up as instructed meaning the staff didnt even attempt to feed her. They just told us that she would not eat them. When they did attempt to feed her it was not enough times throughout the full day.

Staff were instructed not to expose her to direct sunlight as reccomended by the doctor to which they responded "its unavoidable she will be on the grass in the sunlight for certain hours throughout the day". Thats just unacceptable when she has sensitive skin and a doctor advised against it.

The staff have great communication discrepancies between eachother and constantly tell me and my wife different things when speaking to the same and different staff. Theyre extremely poorly coordinated and theres definitely a lack of professionalism between them.

The staff also accused me and my wife of being rude or saying rude things over the phone which we never did. They first asked me and then asked my wife seperately. The management were very argumentative, dismissive, ignorant and disrespectful when speaking to both me and my wife.

Overall I definitely do not reccomend this daycare and anybody considering it should look elsewhere. The staff are all immature and inexperienced, they dont really know what theyre talking about half the time, they do not communicate with eachother, and none of the staff have the ability to answer extremely basic questions in regards to care of children. I believe they put the safety of my daughter at risk on numerous occasions and the things listed above are only the tip of the iceberg for what we experienced throughout her time here.

As a Balkan person I support local businesses especially Balkan businesses but today the owner was so arrogant and disinterested that I felt walking out of the shop with my other 8 family members as the only customers at the shop at the time.
But I didn’t because of a lovely lady that served us food and I also came with my family to celebrate my birthday and support the business in this difficult time.

Shop renovation is  10/10
Food : cevapi supplier changed and they are not bad but over cooked today,lepinja was very good,burek was very good today but also not consistent as burek sometimes is good and sometimes not so good.Also ordered on uber previously and there is inconsistency in cooking.
You might get cevapi cooked perfectly and another cevapi completely over cooked in same order.
Sirnica not to our liking but it was OK
Ajvar was not to our liking but kajmak was good chips was good.

After all food is reasonably still good but the problem is the owner and his attitude.

This is definitely how we don’t treat customers in Travnik if you know what I mean.

Until I get proper response on my review and clear explanation I will never ever come to your store again and as a Balkan person I will make sure I spread the word around to all my Balkan friends.

Extremely poor experience, rude, aggressive and completely unacceptable treatment of a customer.

I am writing this review because I am extremely disappointed and angry about the way my wife was treated at Hair Colosseum Stanhope Gardens.

My wife arrived at approximately 9:10 am and did not leave until around 4pm almost seven hours at the salon. After all that time, she was left with an unfinished haircut because she raised a genuine concern that the haircut was not what she had clearly requested.

She explained what she wanted to Tilly before the service. When she politely asked for the haircut to be corrected, Tilly simply walked away and refused to finish the service.

But the worst part was Scott's behaviour.

Instead of listening to a customer who was unhappy with the result, Scott shouted at my wife and spoke to her in an extremely disrespectful and intimidating manner. He used insulting language, including words to the effect of:

“You’re behaving cheaply. If you want a professional haircut, go somewhere else and pay a premium.”

This is NOT how you speak to a paying customer.

My wife was extremely distressed and intimidated by the way Scott spoke to her. She was already sitting there for hours dealing with an unsatisfactory haircut, and rather than trying to resolve the situation professionally, she was shouted at and made to feel like she was the problem for simply expressing her concerns.

Let me be very clear: customers are not there to be shouted at, insulted or intimidated.

If you cannot handle a customer raising a legitimate concern, you should not be dealing with customers.

Making a mistake with a haircut can happen. Refusing to fix it, abandoning the customer with an unfinished haircut and then shouting at them is a completely different matter.

Scott needs to seriously reconsider the way he speaks to women and customers. Being frustrated does not give anyone the right to raise their voice, insult someone or make them feel intimidated.

The owner/management should seriously review what happened and consider whether this is how they expect customers to be treated when something goes wrong.

We have documented the condition of the haircut and the details of the incident and will be taking the matter through the appropriate consumer complaint channels.

I would strongly advise people to think twice before wasting their money here. A customer should not have to spend seven hours in a salon only to leave with an unfinished haircut, feel humiliated by staff and be afraid to raise a legitimate concern.

Extremely disappointing experience with Zeekr Waterloo/ City Centre.

We ordered our car and paid the deposit at the end of May and are still waiting. Communication throughout the entire process has been terrible — extremely slow responses, messages not responded to, and numerous attempts to call with no one answering the phone.

On the very day we ordered and paid our deposit, I left a voicemail requesting a change to the colour of the car. That voicemail was never responded to. I called several times following that but no one answers the phone. We subsequently had several conversations by phone and text confirming the colour change, only to eventually discover that the paperwork had never been updated and the car arrived in the wrong colour.

Throughout the process we have repeatedly been told the car will be here “soon” or “by the end of the month”. The end of the month comes and goes, there is no car, and we are given another timeframe. In this day and age, it is difficult to understand how there can be so little visibility or communication around expected shipments and delivery dates.

We also asked about going to another Zeekr dealership to see whether they had the vehicle we wanted in stock, but were told we would lose our deposit if we did so. Instead, we have repeatedly been offered other vehicles or upgrades that we simply don’t want.

After waiting since the end of May, the combination of poor communication, unanswered calls, repeated delays, shifting delivery dates and ultimately receiving the wrong colour has made what should have been an exciting experience incredibly frustrating.

Very disappointing service and customer experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible customer service, which is incredibly disappointing because the milk itself is excellent.

My husband and I drove an hour to get here, arriving about 6 minutes before our friends, who came in a separate car. My friend and I each purchased around $50 worth of milk while our husbands waited outside with the cars.

We had been there for no more than 15 minutes in total when an older lady came out and rudely asked if we were still buying, saying “their customers” usually come in and out and we were taking up parking spaces. She then told us that if we wanted to catch up, we should go to a nearby park.

The comment about “their customers” was particularly disappointing. We were customers too, and had just spent around $100 between us after driving an hour specifically to shop there.

It was my friend’s first visit, so she was looking through the selection while I showed her how the payment system worked. We weren’t simply hanging around or using the car park to socialise. We were shopping and had only been there for around 15 minutes.

I understand parking may be limited, but there are far more respectful ways to speak to paying customers.

The milk is genuinely great, but unfortunately we won’t be returning. No product is good enough to justify supporting a business that makes its customers feel unwelcome.
